steps.name: Weary-eyed Gravedigger
steps.text: Hm? How deep are we?

steps.name: Pasty-faced Gravedigger
steps.text: Reckon we should dig a little more?

steps.name: Pasty-faced Gravedigger
steps.text: It'll all be a wasteland here sooner or later. It's not like you could stick wheels under the graves.

steps.name: Pasty-faced Gravedigger
steps.text: Folks want to leave behind some trace of their lives after they die... but it's all a pointless dream, sadly. Might as well ask for a cremation and have your ashes scattered in the wilderness.

steps.name: Weary-eyed Gravedigger
steps.text: That would put us out of a job, though.

steps.name: Pasty-faced Gravedigger
steps.text: True enough.

steps.name: Weary-eyed Gravedigger
steps.text: If you ask me, graves aren't for the dead. It's the living who need these things... The ceremonies and the big chunk of rock that goes on top of them.

steps.name: Weary-eyed Gravedigger
steps.text: Those are the things that folks say their goodbyes to before starting anew—

steps.name: Pasty-faced Gravedigger
steps.text: Hah, until it's their turn to bite the dust.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The preparations for the ritual are almost complete.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I... I'm not sure.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I... I don't feel so good today...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mamma...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar, I was really happy yesterday...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Rosella told me about lots of fun stuff... We prepared for the funeral together, and it felt like... I was doing something for Mamma.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But... we're done with everything now... What comes next?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I think... I worked really hard... for Mamma...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But... can Mamma see all that?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Does all of this... really mean something?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar, have you gone through this a lot?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: When it happens... during... the funeral... what... what should I do?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: And what do I do... once it's over?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Hm. Right, the funeral...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You're still young, but I don't want to hide anything from you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We do a lot of things for others, but, in the end, we do it for ourselves.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Cecelia, this isn't selfishness. Rather, it just means that, ultimately, everything that the living do is to mold and shape themselves.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We hold funerals and say our goodbyes when our loved ones leave us, but it's also a respite for ourselves.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's a way to mark the road that we've trodden.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Many grown-ups... use this as a way to find peace, but whether they truly find it, or indeed anything, isn't the fault of the funeral itself.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's really up to us, after we go through the thing.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Once we are done looking back and resting, we must keep going forward.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But where do we go after that?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That is something you need to ask yourself, Cecelia.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This is a question that only you can answer yourself, and it's a question that both you, I, and everyone must answer in our lifetimes.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Ask myself...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Only you can find the right way forward for yourself, and it is only with your own two legs that you can walk that path.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: What about you, Mister Friar? You know so much... What is your road like?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I can't answer you that. I'm afraid I can't even say I've found it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's a tough search, and a sad journey. It makes you wonder if the way forward ever truly exists.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I haven't given up, and that is why I, and my brothers and sisters, call ourselves...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: ...'the Pathfinders.'

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Candelabra, candelabra. Where does one find...?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: (Somebody's there... That Liberi from the hospital? Patia, was it? And the Legatus called Oren, too.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I really don't get it. What is that guy even doing?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Watch your words, Oren.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: This is the perfect time to act. There are lots of other things we could be doing besides wasting time on a funeral.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: And I thought you were close to the girl's mother. How cold-blooded of you.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I'd already made my decision when I told Andoain about Cecelia.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: She's capable of knocking this city off its godly throne.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: That also means she can shake that saint who's always hiding behind the red and gold curtain... and plenty of others besides.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: (What is he talking about?)

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: A Sankta wants to bring down his holy city with the help of a mixed-blood girl? Scandalous.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You make it sound like I just want to burn it all down for no good reason. I said 'capable.' That doesn't mean we have to do it.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: In fact, if we don't do it, then her worth as a bargaining chip is that much more.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I just have to make sure Cecelia doesn't end up in the Pope's hands... On that point at least, Andoain and I are aligned.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: A word of advice.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: I don't know what kind of tricks you're trying to play with Cecelia, but do not forget the promise you made to the Guide.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Thanks for the tip... I don't mind walking this path with you folks for a little longer.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Now, you'll have to excuse me. I have better places to be than a funeral.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: (Looks like they aren't all on the same wavelength.)

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: (But what worries me more... is that there's a Legatus involved.)

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: (I'll take Cecelia and leave once the funeral is over.)

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Cecelia. Cecelia!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Senior Ezell, the funeral will be starting soon.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Andoain, I don't care about your grand ideals, and I'm not interested in discussing faith with you.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: So once the funeral is over... I'm leaving with Cecelia.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Where will you go?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: None of your concern.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's time to light the candles, Senior Ezell. Go, be with Cecelia.
The early spring mornings are still frigid here in Laterano.
Sankta funerals are often accompanied by laughter, music, sweets, and the occasional, inconsequential explosion.
The departed become one with the Holy Spirit and return to Heaven. This is worthy of celebration.
But there is another kind of Sankta 'funeral' unknown to other races:
On a certain hour of a certain day, a great sorrow will seize all Sankta by the throat. They will not be able to move, breathe, or avert their eyes.
Each and every fragile soul will be swept away as if by the floodwaters of a broken dam.
Yet neither the joy of the former nor the awesome power of the latter can be found today in the Ecclesia Requietum of Pagus Stevonus.
We find only a frail girl, trying her hardest to swing the absurdly unwieldy shovel in her hands.
A girl trying to shovel the last bit of dirt onto her mother's resting place.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Go, Cecelia. It's time to see goodbye.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mamma... What should I do?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: When I think to myself that... I'm doing this for Mamma, I don't feel scared of anything... I feel like I can do anything.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: It feels like I've gotten a little stronger since you've been gone... Is it because I got a little older?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But Mister Ezell says... I won't get to see you anymore. Even if I grow up and grow even stronger, I won't see you again... right?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: When I do a good job, you won't be there to reward me... When I do something bad, you won't be there to get angry at me...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: So, why should I grow up?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar says... I'm doing your funeral and saying goodbye to you... for myself...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: What does it mean to do something for myself?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I'm scared... Mamma...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: A few days ago, a prioress lady that I don't know told me that, whether we do it with tears or smiles, the ones who are leaving us will accept our goodbyes.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I don't get it... Mamma, should I cry, or should I smile?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar said it's a question for myself... but I... I don't know...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There is no rush, Cecelia.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You still have lots of time.
Too bad, then, that yours just ran out.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hey, been a while.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I've finally got you, Andoain.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Mostima, Fiammetta... my dear old friends, long time no see.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If you're here to mourn the dead, I'm afraid you came a little too late.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: That's alright.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We can always make some more.
